objetivo.en: Give recipe instructions to one person with usted and to several people with ustedes.

nota.en: Fresh corn on the cob, very common in Ecuador and Peru.

explicacion.en: Señora Rosa is someone you address with usted, so the command is corte, not corta. Corta is for a friend (tú).

explicacion.en: When you speak to two or more people, add -n to the usted command: corten, not corte.
To tell one person with usted not to do something, use no + the usted command (añada). Añade is the tú command.

texto.en: In a kitchen and on a recipe card you give instructions with a command (the imperative). For one person you treat as usted (señora Rosa, don Jorge, the reader of a recipe card), the command changes the vowel of the present tense: -ar verbs take -e (cortar → corte, pelar → pele, mezclar → mezcle) and -er/-ir verbs take -a (añadir → añada, servir → sirva). For several people (ustedes), add -n to the usted form: corten, pelen, añadan, mezclen, sirvan. Poner is irregular: ponga, pongan. To say not to do something, put no before the same form: no añada sal todavía. Do not mix it up with tú, which is a different form (corta, añade, pela): Rosa says «Corta la cebolla» to Daniela alone, but «Corten la cebolla» to Emma and Daniela together.
The verb stays the same; only the person you talk to changes the ending. Tap each form to hear it.

objetivo.en: Give commands with pronouns to one person (usted), to several people (ustedes) and to a friend (córtelo, sírvanse, pásamelo).

explicacion.en: In an affirmative command the pronoun attaches to the end of the verb: pruébelo. Before the verb (lo pruebe) it is only for the negative: no lo pruebe.
Don Jorge is someone you address with usted, so the command is pruébelo, not pruébalo. Pruébalo is for a friend (tú).
When a pronoun joins the command, the stress stays on the same syllable and a written accent appears: PRUÉ-be-lo, pruébelo.

texto.en: In an affirmative command the pronoun attaches to the end of the verb, and a written accent keeps the stress where it was: corte → córtelo, pruebe → pruébelo, sirva → sírvase. With ustedes the pronoun goes after the -n: córtenlo, pruébenlo, sírvanse. With a friend (tú): córtalo, pruébalo, sírvete. In a negative command the pronoun goes before the verb and is separate: no lo corte, no se sirva. Two pronouns can join too: the one for the person comes first, then lo or la. So pasa + me + lo = pásamelo (pass it to me), and pasa + me + la = pásamela. Lo is for a masculine thing (el ají) and la for a feminine one (la sal).
The pronoun joins the end of an affirmative command. Tap each form to hear it.

explicacion.en: English says “is served” without any extra word, but Spanish needs se in front of the verb: se sirve.

titulo.en: How a dish is made: se + verb

texto.en: To explain how something is done without saying who does it, Spanish uses se + the verb in the third person. It works like the English passive: se corta la cebolla = the onion is chopped. The verb agrees with what is being done: one thing, se corta la cebolla; several things, se cortan las papas. You see it in recipes, menus and signs: se sirve caliente (it is served hot), se come con arroz (it is eaten with rice). Compare with the command from the last lessons: Corte la cebolla tells someone to do it; Se corta la cebolla just describes how the dish is made.
One thing → se + verb. Several things → se + verb + n. Tap each form to hear it.

objetivo.en: Book a table and order in a restaurant politely (¿Podría…?, me gustaría…).

nota.en: In a restaurant, la carta is the menu.

explicacion.en: Puedes is tú, which is for friends. With a waiter you don't know, use usted and the softer form: ¿Podría traerme…?

explicacion.en: Me gusta says you like something. To ask politely for what you want, use me gustaría (I would like).

erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Quería reservar una mesa para cuatro.

explicacion.en: Quiero sounds blunt on the phone. Quería reservar… or ¿Podría reservar…? is more polite.

texto.en: To ask for something politely, Spanish softens the verb. With a person you don't know, such as a receptionist or a waiter (usted), use ¿Podría + infinitive?: ¿Podría traerme la carta? (Could you bring me the menu?). With a friend (tú) it is ¿Podrías + infinitive?. To say what you would like, use me gustaría + a noun or an infinitive: me gustaría el seco de pollo (I would like the chicken stew), me gustaría reservar para el sábado (I would like to book for Saturday). Podría is the same for “I” and for “you” (usted), so the situation decides: ¿Podría reservar una mesa? means “Could I book a table?”, while ¿Podría traerme la carta? means “Could you bring me the menu?”. You can attach me (to me) or nos (to us) to the infinitive: traerme, traernos. You already know quería from the last lesson: Quería reservar una mesa is another polite opener on the phone.
The same request, to a stranger and to a friend. Tap each phrase to hear it.

objetivo.en: Describe how a dish tastes (está rico, está salado) and tell how something is by nature from how it is right now.

nota.en: With estar: está rico = it tastes good. Feminine: rica.
Ends in -e: the same for masculine and feminine.
Ends in -e: the same for masculine and feminine.
Plural: crujientes.

explicacion.en: Es salada would mean the soup is salty by nature, always. To say it tastes too salty right now, use está.
The adjective agrees with the noun, not with the verb: sopa is feminine, so salada. The same happens with ser: el ají es picante, la sopa es salada.
The adjective agrees with the noun: one thing, crujiente; several things, crujientes.

titulo.en: Es or está: always or right now?

texto.en: Use estar for how a dish tastes or how hot or cold it is right now: la sopa está salada, el café está frío, está muy rico. It describes this soup, this cup, this moment. Use ser for what something is like by nature, always: el ají es picante, el limón es ácido. Put muy or un poco before the adjective: muy salada, un poco dulce. The adjective agrees with the noun: la sopa está fría, el café está frío, las papas están crujientes. Adjectives ending in -e (dulce, picante, caliente, crujiente) have the same form for masculine and feminine, and add -s in the plural.
Same adjective, two verbs. Tap each phrase to hear it.

columnas.en: Ser: how it is by nature

traduccion.en: The soup is salty. (right now, too much)

items.texto: El seco de pollo está muy rico.

traduccion.en: The chicken stew is very good. (it tastes great)

items.texto: El postre está un poco dulce.

traduccion.en: The dessert is a little sweet.

items.texto: Esta sopa está fría. ¿Podría traerme otra, por favor?

traduccion.en: This soup is cold. Could you bring me another one, please?

consigna.en: The soup tastes too salty right now. Choose.

feedback.en: A taste right now: está.

consigna.en: Complete (always spicy by nature): “Chili sauce is spicy.”

feedback.en: By nature: es.

consigna.en: Complete (right now): “The coffee is cold.”

feedback.en: Right now: está.

consigna.en: Choose the correct form: “The potatoes are crispy.”

feedback.en: Papas is plural, so crujientes.

consigna.en: Listen. How is the dessert?

feedback.en: Muy dulce: very sweet.

consigna.en: Match each flavor word with its meaning.

feedback.en: Salado, dulce, picante and ácido are four basic flavors.

consigna.en: Put in order: “The soup is very hot.”

feedback.en: La sopa está muy caliente.

consigna.en: Write in Spanish (use está): “The dessert is very sweet.”

feedback.en: A taste right now: está muy dulce.

contexto.en: Saturday night at the restaurant in La Mariscal. Emma, Daniela and Mateo use tú with each other. They taste their dishes. Emma's soup is too salty and she politely asks the Mesero (usted) for another one.

dialogo.texto: Mi seco de pollo está muy rico. ¿Y tu sopa, Emma?

traduccion.en: My chicken stew is very good. And your soup, Emma?

dialogo.texto: Un momento... Está muy salada.

traduccion.en: One moment... It is very salty.

dialogo.texto: Mi arroz está un poco frío, pero el ají es muy picante.

traduccion.en: My rice is a little cold, but the chili sauce is very spicy.

dialogo.texto: Señor, ¿podría traerme otra sopa, por favor?

traduccion.en: Sir, could you bring me another soup, please?

dialogo.texto: Sí, claro, señorita. Perdón, un momento, por favor.

traduccion.en: Yes, of course, miss. Sorry, one moment, please.

dialogo.texto: Aquí está su sopa. ¿Cómo está ahora?

traduccion.en: Here is your soup. How is it now?

dialogo.texto: Ahora está muy rica, gracias.

traduccion.en: Now it is very good, thank you.

dialogo.texto: ¡Qué bien! Y el postre, ¿cómo está? Yo quiero un postre dulce.

traduccion.en: Great! And the dessert, how is it? I want a sweet dessert.

consigna.en: In the dialogue, what is wrong with Emma's soup?

feedback.en: Emma says: «Está muy salada».

consigna.en: In the dialogue, how is Mateo's chicken stew?

feedback.en: Mateo says: «Mi seco de pollo está muy rico».

consigna.en: The soup tastes cold right now. Choose.

feedback.en: A temperature right now: está fría.

consigna.en: Complete (right now): “The chicken stew is delicious.”

feedback.en: Right now: está.

consigna.en: Put in order: “This soup is very salty.”

feedback.en: Esta sopa está muy salada.

consigna.en: Listen. Does the speaker describe how it is by nature or how it is right now?

feedback.en: El limón es ácido uses es: by nature.

consigna.en: (Open) Write 15 words or more in Spanish: describe the soup and the dessert with es or está and politely ask the waiter (usted) to replace the soup.

feedback.en: Model: está muy salada, está un poco dulce, ¿Podría traerme otra sopa? Any version with at least 15 words is fine.

items.respuesta: La sopa está muy salada y el postre está un poco dulce. ¿Podría traerme otra sopa, por favor? El ají es picante.
